Folks — quick read of Acme's redlines. Proposed path: keep MSA confidentiality intact and add a short Order Form addendum along these lines (high level):

--- Proposed addendum language (draft) ---
1. Customer may reference Supplier (Redwood Inference) by name in Customer press materials limited to a single announcement and a single attributable quote provided such quote is pre-approved in writing by Supplier in accordance with the approval process set forth below.
2. Use of Supplier trademarks (logo) in Customer marketing materials is permitted for a period of twelve (12) months from the live date for placement on Customer-owned web pages only; any third-party distribution or resale is prohibited. Supplier approval required on final artwork; Supplier to provide approval/feedback within forty-eight (48) hours of submission.
3. No confidential technical, performance, or pricing information may be disclosed as part of any public reference or quote unless expressly approved in writing by Supplier.
4. Customer shall provide Supplier with a reasonable evidence package (copy of press release, final web URL, and creative) at least seven (7) business days prior to publication for Supplier review.
--- end draft ---

Rationale: this keeps the MSA confidentiality protections and limits the exposure by (a) restricting to one announcement, (b) requiring prior approval and a short evidence package, and (c) prohibiting disclosure of any confidential metrics unless separately approved.

Marcus — from a marketing/brand perspective, this is standard; confirm that 48 hours is workable for approval and if they need a small logo asset pack (PNG, SVG) we'll supply a brand-safe zip once the flow is agreed.

Mina — if procurement insists on including an explicit indemnity related to press, we'll need to push back; recommend we avoid indemnity language and keep approval/timebox controls. If they insist, we'll route to Legal Ops for escalation.

If everyone agrees I can redline the PDF and return to Acme. Sophie — is that acceptable as a starting point?

Thanks,
Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
